subject: Operational readiness & incident flow - content moderation RFI
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fintrue.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: security@fintrue.com; procurement@fintrue.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operational readiness & incident flow - content moderation (RFI)

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking our RFI. As part of our diligence we need a concise operational readiness description for content moderation and misuse detection. Specifically can you provide: 1) the incident detection -> escalation -> resolution flow for a high-severity policy violation (example: coordinated disinformation campaign detected), 2) average detection latency and alerting thresholds for production models, 3) sample alert payloads and runbooks your SOC uses, and 4) SLAs for response/mitigation across tiers.

We have an upcoming vendor review next week; a short written response plus any artifacts you can share (matrix, playbook excerpt) would be most helpful. If you have a redacted example incident timeline that would be ideal.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Security Operations
FinTrue

--
FinTrue (external partner)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fintrue.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational readiness & incident flow - content moderation (RFI)

Hi Elaine —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've attached a short excerpt from our Moderation Playbook and a Monitoring Matrix that map detection triggers to escalation paths and remediation options. The excerpt contains a redacted incident timeline we can share. High level answers below; we'll follow up with a more technical annex next week (cc: Markus & Rishi).

1) Incident flow (summary): detection -> automated triage (confidence/risk scoring) -> SOC alert -> human review & taxonomy tagging -> mitigation action (rate-limit/block/model fallback) -> customer notification & post-mortem. Playbook excerpt has the diagram and decision thresholds.

2) Detection latency: for our hosted models median detection (signal generation + scoring) is ~800ms for conversational requests; end-to-end detection-to-alert (including batching and enrichment) typically runs 1.2–3s depending on traffic patterns and sampling, with configurable sampling windows. For large coordinated signals we also run streaming n-gram/embedding aggregation jobs (minute-resolution).

3) Sample alert payloads/runbooks: see Monitoring_Matrix_v2.xlsx (tab: Alerts) and playbook excerpt (section 3). Alerts include severity, model signature, sample input, confidence score, user id (hashed), and suggested mitigation actions.

4) SLAs: our standard incident response windows are documented in SLA_Tiered_Resp_Times.docx (attached) — P1: initial ack within 30 minutes, mitigation plan within 4 hours; P2: ack within 4 hours; P3: ack within 24 hours. For Dedicated/Enterprise customers we offer tighter SLAs under contract.

If okay, I'd like to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with the SOC and product security next week to walk through the playbook and the redacted timeline. Proposed times Tuesday/Wednesday afternoon PST.

Attachments: Redwood_Moderation_Playbook_excerpt.pdf (redacted), Monitoring_Matrix_v2.xlsx, SLA_Tiered_Resp_Times.docx

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference | developer-first high-performance LLM inference

Subject: Re: Operational readiness & incident flow - content moderation (RFI)

Monica / team —

Couple of quick clarifications we should include in the annex to Elaine:
- Detection scoring: specify model-level vs. ensemble scoring and how we derive the composite confidence. Note we do a secondary pattern detection pass for high-volume anomalies (embeddings clustering).
- Audit trail: confirm retention windows for original request, model logits, and moderation decisions (30/90/365 days depending on contract).
- Human review SLA: mention expected human-review throughput per reviewer and on-call rotation for P1s.
- Escalation to legal/compliance: provide criteria (user harm threshold, regulatory trigger) and example notification templates.

I drafted a short annex and a redacted timeline example (local doc) — Monica can you attach the annex & call invite? I'll also pull a sample alert JSON from observability for them to inspect (remove PII).

-Markus
Director, Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a consolidated response and a short annex with sample alert JSON and the redacted incident timeline Markus referenced. I pasted the key excerpts below for quick review.

Excerpt (sample alert JSON):
{
  "alert_id": "redwood-20261201-9421",
  "severity": "P1",
  "model_signature": "toxicity-ensemble-v3",
  "confidence": 0.96,
  "sample_input": "[redacted]",
  "first_detected_at": "2026-12-01T02:17:42Z",
  "suggested_action": ["rate_limit_user","escalate_to_human_review"]
}

Redacted timeline (summary):
- 00:00 detection: ensemble spike + embedding-cluster detected across ~450 requests
- 00:00-00:03 auto-triage: confidence 0.94 -> P1 flagged
- 00:30 human review confirmed coordinated misinfo; mitigation: model fallback + user rate-limit
- 03:00 automated rollback of a noisy prompt cache; 12:00 internal post-mortem created

Key SLAs (summary): P1 ack <30m, mitigation plan <4h, full remediation & report within 72h (scope-dependent). Enterprise customers can contract for forensic evidence retention and dedicated on-call rotations.

Attachments: Redwood_Moderation_Playbook_excerpt.pdf, Monitoring_Matrix_v2.xlsx, SLA_Tiered_Resp_Times.docx

I also created a short HubSpot note and attached the annex there: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FT-2026-0912. If the artifacts look good I'll push the DocuSign for our standard enterprise data addendum (link below).
